Houthis claim missile strike on Saudi Forces in Jazan
sum: Sanaa, Nov 14: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group on Friday claimed to have fired two ballistic missiles at what it described as concentrations of Saudi forces in Al-Tuwal, in the Jazan province of Saudi Arabia.
The claim came hours after Saudi civil defence authorities issued an all-clear for the province. It was not immediately clear whether the reported missile attack was connected to the earlier alerts.

Jazan is home to a Saudi Aramco refinery with a capacity to process 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day. Southern Saudi Arabia, which shares a border with Yemen, has repeatedly faced Houthi missile and drone attacks targeting military installations and energy infrastructure, including the Jazan refinery.

In a separate statement, the Houthis also claimed to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a pumping station along Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the claims.

Amid disruptions to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz due to the ongoing Middle East conflict, Saudi Arabia has diverted around four million barrels of crude oil per day through the East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This accounts for approximately four per cent of global oil supply.

Meanwhile, fighting between the Houthis and the coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government has intensified. The escalation follows the Houthi advance in September towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic shipping route at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.

items.t: DRTECH's bendable detector approved for use by Saudi Aramco and ADNOC
sum: DRTECH said Thursday that it has received final end-user approval from Saudi Aramco and the United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) for its bendable X-ray detectors, which convert X-ray images into digital data.
The company plans to accelerate its push into the global industrial nondestructive testing (NDT) market.
DRTECH said the approvals from the two state-owned oil companies validate the performance of its proprietary bendable detectors for industrial applications.

Until now, film-based analog methods have dominated inspections of pipeline welds. The company expects the approvals to accelerate the adoption of digital NDT solutions, which offer greater inspection efficiency.

DRTECH has been expanding its bendable detector lineup through active research and development. It has developed 4-inch, 8-inch and 16-inch models and recently introduced a compact 2-inch model for inspecting small-diameter pipelines. The expanded lineup allows the company to serve a wide range of pipeline sizes, from small to large diameters.

The company is also expanding supplies of its bendable detectors in North America. Earlier this year, it supplied a 16-inch model for inspecting large-diameter pipelines to Company A, the region's largest specialized NDT provider. It recently secured additional approval to supply a new model capable of inspecting small-diameter pipelines as narrow as 2 inches.

Company A has annual revenue of 1.6 trillion won and provides NDT and facility management services across various industries, including oil and gas, shipbuilding, chemicals and aerospace, primarily in the United States and Canada.

Intuitive Machines Surges 16% on Record Quarter and Positive Free Cash Flow; AST SpaceMobile Falls 3%, Rocket Lab Slips 2%
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

A record quarter is pulling Intuitive Machines (NASDAQ:LUNR) away from the rest of the space group amid a broad pullback in growth stocks. Intuitive Machines stock is at $14.19, up 16% in early morning trading. The company released its Q3 2026 results before the open on November 12 and beat expectations on both revenue and loss per share.

Third-quarter revenue at Intuitive Machines reached $269.35 million, exceeding the $247.56 million consensus estimate and rising 413.7% from a year earlier. Satellite production from the January Lanteris acquisition drove most of that growth, adding $215.12 million of revenue. CEO Steve Altemus declared, “In the third quarter, we delivered record financial performance across the board.”

Cash generation sets this report apart. Intuitive Machines produced operating cash flow of $66 million and free cash flow of $33 million, a record. Backlog at the company climbed to a record $1.87 billion from $213 million at December 31, 2025.

NASA also named Intuitive Machines a vendor on its $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) 2 contract. Looking ahead, Intuitive Machines expects full-year 2026 revenue of $920 million to $950 million along with positive adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.

Skeptics have reasons for caution about Intuitive Machines. A $30.01 million gain from the change in fair value of warrant liabilities helped the company post a loss of $0.02 per share, narrower than the $0.11 loss analysts expected. Acquisition costs and a non-recurring legal expense partly offset that gain, yet the company’s $34.2 million operating loss shows the core business still isn’t profitable.
One-time program adjustments also raised gross margin at Intuitive Machines. Free cash flow at the company stands at negative $112.3 million year to date, even after the strong quarter.

Tankers continue to burn in the Middle East despite hopes for de-escalation, Asia News
sum: Despite market bets on a de-escalation in the Iran war, new evidence has emerged in recent days of strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and on energy infrastructure in the Middle East.

On Tuesday (Nov 10), crude prices hit two-month lows after US officials downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the Republicans' defeat in the Nov 3 midterm elections.

However, there is little sign of attacks abating in November, after 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.

Videos posted on social media on Sunday and verified by Reuters showed a Navig8 tanker on fire near the coast of Oman. An image captured by the European Union's Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite on Sunday showed a large cloud of black smoke at the same location.
It was one of three tankers hit on Sunday for using "unauthorised routes" through the strait, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported, citing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy.
The vessel is managed by Navig8, majority owned by ADNOC Logistics & Services. Neither replied to emailed Reuters requests for comment.

At the same time, US forces continued to enforce a naval blockade of Iranian ports. In the latest incident, a US military aircraft fired on and disabled a St Kitts-flagged cargo vessel that tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port on Saturday, US Central Command said.

Saudi-led coalition reports Houthi missile, drone interceptions; Saba reports Saudi strikes on Sanaa
sum: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Tuesday (Nov 10) it intercepted two missiles launched by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis towards Riyadh, a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's southern region and a drone over its oil-rich Eastern Province, in a night of heightened military activity across Saudi Arabia.

The latest launches come amid an escalation in hostilities between the Houthis and the coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government after the group advanced in September towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic shipping chokepoint at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.
The Houthis have since stepped up strikes on Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities, while Saudi Arabia has carried out airstrikes on Houthi targets in Yemen.

The coalition said its air defences had destroyed a ballistic missile and a cruise missile fired towards the Saudi capital. Saudi Civil Defence had earlier issued an early-warning alert for Riyadh before later saying the threat had passed.
In a separate statement, the coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched towards southern Saudi Arabia, which borders Yemen.
Saudi Civil Defence had previously issued warning alerts for the southwestern cities of Abha and Khamis Mushait, before later saying the danger had passed.

The Houthi-run Saba news agency reported that Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes on Yemen's Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, hitting the al-Mufazir gas station in the Jadar district north of the capital and a building belonging to the state oil company in southern Sanaa.

sum: Saudi Arabia's civil defence on Sunday (Nov 8) lifted alerts in several areas of the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province, including Dhahran, home to the headquarters of oil major Saudi Aramco, shortly after warning of potential danger.
The all-clear also applies to Dammam, Abqaiq and Al-Ahsa governorate, the civil defence said.
The Eastern Province contains the majority of the kingdom's oil and gas reserves as well as Saudi Aramco's headquarters, which suffered extensive damage in an attack in October.
Shortly after the all-clear, the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Yemeni Iran-allied Houthi group towards the Eastern region.

The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in a war that began with the US and Israel attacking Iran in February.

Oil Rebounds Toward $100 as Democrats' Sweep Rattles Energy Stocks
sum: Oil prices reversed their recent downtrend on Thursday, a day after Democrats swept control of both the House and Senate, creating a potential legislative check on U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration. Brent crude was up 4.0% to trade at $98.38 per barrel at 3:15 pm ET, while WTI gained 2.9% to $90.65, with prices rising for the first time in four sessions after plunging to a near two-month low on Wednesday. U.S. natural gas prices were flat at $2.95/MMBtu, while European gas prices rebounded 1.9% to €89.72/MWh. The U.S. stock market resumed its recent downtrend on Thursday, with the S&P 500 down more than 3% and the Nasdaq off about 5% in afternoon trading as a selloff in AI chip stocks deepened. AI stocks tied to Texas data centers were hit hard after Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated long-serving Texas governor Greg Abbott, with CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) falling 7% and Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) and Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) each sliding 4% in overnight trading on Wednesday. Hinojosa has called for a pause on new data-center projects until protections for electricity supplies, water resources and local communities are in place, with investors fearing similar roadblocks could slow down the AI data center boom once Democratic governors take office in January 2027.

The energy investment universe was a mixed bag, with the oil and gas benchmark, State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), falling 1.6% to $62.50 on Thursday, as energy stocks tracked the broader market lower despite the rebound in crude. Wednesday’s 8.7% plunge in Brent priced in bets that the election setback would force the Trump administration to pursue a peace deal with Iran and reopen Hormuz.

Those bets faded on Thursday, with Eurasia Group cutting its odds of a negotiated agreement to 10% from 20% and putting the likelihood of renewed U.S. strikes at 60%, while Iran’s navy reported that a tanker struck a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire. President Trump acknowledged the war’s role in the Republican losses but said the conflict has been worth it.
Additionally, Democratic committee chairs are set to deploy their new subpoena powers from January to investigate the administration’s energy dealings.

items.t: 3 Private Deals Executed on the Saudi Stock Exchange, Valued at SAR 49 Million
sum: On Monday, November 2, 2026, three private deals were executed on the Saudi Stock Exchange ("Tadawul"), involving 2.2 million shares of Saudi Aramco, Saudi Electrical Industries, and AlAhli Bank. The total value of these transactions reached approximately SAR 49 million.

A private transaction occurs when both the seller and the buyer agree upon the quantity and price of the listed securities involved. Regarding settlement, these negotiated transactions can be settled within a timeframe ranging from T+0 to T+5, as agreed upon by the parties; if no specific settlement period is determined by the seller and buyer, a T+2 settlement cycle is applied automatically.

Furthermore, transactions executed during any additional trading sessions must comply with daily price fluctuation limits and minimum transaction value requirements. Negotiated transactions may be carried out during the following sessions: the pre-opening auction, the open market session, the closing auction, the market-closed session, and the post-closing session.

The pre-opening auction and post-closing sessions are made available once the lead underwriter or the transaction coordinator submits a formal request and fulfills all requirements set by the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) for enabling these sessions.

Google, Nvidia Led $3.17T AI Stock Slide; Only Four Rose
sum: Thirty large AI-exposed stocks lost a combined $3.17 trillion of market value in October, from $37.53 trillion at the end of September to $34.36 trillion at the close on 30 October, an 8.5% fall by our arithmetic. Only four of the 30 rose.

Alphabet, Google’s parent, and Nvidia together lost $1.35 trillion, 43% of the total. The gainers were Tesla, Apple, Microsoft and IBM, and the month ended on the day Apple passed Nvidia as the most valuable company.
A short Business Engineer explainer on power laws, where a few outcomes account for most of the value. It teaches the general idea only and does not discuss the companies in this story.

By our arithmetic, Alphabet lost $780.2 billion (18.5%), Nvidia $572.1 billion (10.4%), Intel $289.5 billion (45.3%), Meta $281.7 billion (15.2%) and Micron $204.1 billion (16.9%). Those five account for $2.13 trillion, or 67% of the group’s fall.

Memory makers fell together: Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics lost a combined $549.5 billion. Chip-equipment makers Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA and ASML lost $350.9 billion between them.

The steepest percentage falls were Intel at 45.3%, CoreWeave at 37.0%, Arm at 28.9% and Lam Research at 27.2%. Intel’s shares fell 28.6% on 30 October alone after its results, as we reported on Friday.
Tesla added $177.9 billion (12.7%), Apple $169.4 billion (3.5%), Microsoft $66.9 billion (1.8%) and IBM $35.8 billion (17.2%), by our arithmetic. Salesforce was close to flat, down $0.3 billion.

sum: Saudi Aramco shares rose 4.1% at the close of trading on Sunday, March 8, 2026, settling at SAR 26.94 per share, marking their highest closing price in over a year, specifically since March 3, 2025. This strong surge is supported by a jump in global oil prices (Brent crude surpassed $92) and escalating geopolitical tensions, boosting the performance of energy sector stocks and fueling expectations of strong earnings.
Aramco holds a leading position as one of the world's largest energy and chemicals companies, contributing to global trade and improving the daily lives of millions of people worldwide.

Despite geopolitical challenges, Saudi Aramco possesses strategic alternatives for exporting oil to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, most notably the Petroline (East-West) pipeline, which transports crude oil to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea. This expansion enables the export of approximately 5-7 million barrels per day westward, in addition to relying on strategic Asian reserves to ensure continued supply.

Saudi Aramco is the world’s most reliable energy supplier, with a proven track record of delivering no shipments to its customers for operational reasons in over 90 years. It is committed to a 99.9% supply reliability rate, maintaining its position as the world’s largest integrated energy company and demonstrating its ability to respond quickly to supply challenges, as evidenced by its handling of past operational crises.
Its historical record includes: no shipments delayed for operational reasons in 90 years, and a 99.9% supply reliability rate across its refining, chemicals, and marketing sector.
